item.title: Talasea LLG feeder road maintained
item.description: The upgrading of a feeder road in the Talasea Local Level Government area of West New Britain Province is now assisting locals to easily transport their cash crops to markets in Kimbe Town. The Talasea District Development Authority Board provided funding totaling K580,000 to upgrade the 2.6 kilometre Dami One Feeder Road located in the Ward 10 area of Talasea LLG.
item.content:encoded:
The upgrading of a feeder road in the Talasea Local Level Government area of West New Britain Province is now assisting locals to easily transport their cash crops to markets in Kimbe Town.

The Talasea District Development Authority Board provided funding totaling K580,000 to upgrade the 2.6 kilometre Dami One Feeder Road located in the Ward 10 area of Talasea LLG.

Talasea MP, Freddie Reu Kumai officiated at the official opening of the feeder road today.

He told the gathering at Dami One that the upgrading of the feeder road now provides easy access for them to markets in Kimbe.

"For the past 40 years, you have been neglected by successive governments in terms of the maintenance of your feeder roads. You must now make use of the improved road conditions to sell your cash crops like copra and improve your lives," Kumai said.

Kumai also outlined plans to link up all feeder roads in the Talasea LLG to the main Talasea Ring Road.

item.title: Madang Technical college introduces down-linking concept to Pai vocational centre
item.description: Madang technical college is helping Pai Vocational Centre in Tari, Hela Province, create an educational and training pathway for its students through a new concept that it has developed. The concept is called down-linking, and its primary aim is to encourage and give hope to Tari students to continue their higher certificate and diploma studies at Madang Technical College after completing their TV
item.content:encoded:
Madang technical college is helping Pai Vocational Centre in Tari, Hela Province, create an educational and training pathway for its students through a new concept that it has developed.

The concept is called down-linking, and its primary aim is to encourage and give hope to Tari students to continue their higher certificate and diploma studies at Madang Technical College after completing their TVET and FODE studies.

Last week, the college's Deputy Principal, Administration, Robert Turik, and Deputy Principal, Academic, Herman Bangu visited Pai Vocational Centre to introduce the concept.

Bangu is also head of the welding and drafting department and cabinet making and joinery department.

Turik said the students at Pai vocational centre were excited with the concept.

"The concept will give hope to the young people of Tari to take up TVET and FODE studies because they will create an opportunity for them to move onto Madang Technical College for their higher certificates and diploma studies," he said.

The staff and students at the Pai Vocational Centre were very happy with the opportunity, which they said was a first- of- its- kind.

They were particularly impressed that a far- away school in the coastal region has proposed a concept to an institution in the upper Highlands.

Turik said teachers from Pai TVET will pay a return visit to Madang Technical College soon to see how the programs are run.

"During last week's visit, dialogue was established for the TVET teachers to visit Madang Technical College in November to gain exposure and more understanding of TVET teaching using Competency Base Teaching & Assessment (CBT&A).

"We will also help them with training curriculum, as well as develop programs for them," he added.

Pai Vocational Centre is part of Hope Institute, a privately run educational institution in Tari.

Besides TVET training, Hope Institute also runs a Flexibe Open Distance Education (FODE) centre, creating greater educational advantages for young people.

The students were excited and were challenged by the TVET manager to complete their TVET and FODE studies in order to be able to apply for the studies at Madang Technical College.

Turik said application forms were also given out to the students and Madang Tech is looking forward to enrol its first students next year under the Down-Linking concept should they meet the requirements.

The college has already established similar partnerships with TVET schools in other provinces like East New Britain and Manus.

item.title: Milne Bay family of three burnt to death in brutal attack
item.description: ‎A family of three was burnt to death after more than 15 alleged criminals attacked their home in Yapowa Village, Milne Bay Province, in the early hours of Monday morning. The victims, a father, mother and their 25-year-old son, were at their home in Maramatana Local Level Government, Alotau District, when the attackers allegedly stormed the house demanding food and valuables.
item.content:encoded:
‎A family of three was burnt to death after more than 15 alleged criminals attacked their home in Yapowa Village, Milne Bay Province, in the early hours of Monday morning.

The victims, a father, mother and their 25-year-old son, were at their home in Maramatana Local Level Government, Alotau District, when the attackers allegedly stormed the house demanding food and valuables.

The victims have been identified as 56-year-old Karrybert Frank, his 55-year-old wife, Tracy Frank, and their 25-year-old son, Derek Frank.

Milne Bay Provincial Police Commander Chief Inspector Benjamin Kua said the attackers entered the family’s home at about 3am on Monday.

Kua said the father and son were repeatedly stabbed with crowbars and iron rods, while Tracy was also beaten with metal rods as she tried to protect her family.

He said the family was still inside the house when the attackers set it on fire, killing all three.

Meanwhile, Kua said one suspect was apprehended by community members and severely beaten, with his hands reportedly chopped off. The suspect later died from blood loss while being taken to hospital.

A second suspect has also been apprehended and is now in police custody at Alotau Police Station as investigations continue.

The bodies of the three victims are currently at the Alotau Provincial Morgue.

Alotau MP Ricky Morris has condemned the killings and called on those involved in criminal activities to stop what he described as malicious, greedy, inhuman and illegal acts.

Morris has also called on the Police Commissioner to intervene and support a joint police operation. He pledged that the Alotau District would provide logistical and financial support.

He said those responsible for the killings must be arrested and held accountable under the full force of the law

item.title: Bob Morris remembered as ‘football Icon’ and ‘mentor’ to football generations
item.description: Late football coach, Bob Maiya Morris; has been remembered for his outstanding contributions to soccer in Madang and across Papua New Guinea, with Madang Soccer Association President, Siegfried Beschel; describing his passing as a great loss to PNG football. Speaking during a farewell tribute at Laiwaden Oval in Madang, Beschel said Morris had contributed immensely to the development of soccer thr
item.content:encoded:
Late football coach, Bob Maiya Morris; has been remembered for his outstanding contributions to soccer in Madang and across Papua New Guinea, with Madang Soccer Association President, Siegfried Beschel; describing his passing as a great loss to PNG football.

Speaking during a farewell tribute at Laiwaden Oval in Madang, Beschel said Morris had contributed immensely to the development of soccer through his years of service as a player, coach and mentor to young footballers.

“His passing is a great loss to Madang and Papua New Guinea football, but his legacy will continue through the players he mentored,” Beschel said.

He acknowledged the support of sponsors, football associations, clubs, and individuals who contributed towards hosting the late Morris' haus krai, funeral expenses, and travel costs.

Among those acknowledged were the Papua New Guinea Football Association (PNGFA), Agmark FC, Morobe Wawens, Lae City FC, Madang United FC, other local football clubs and individuals who supported the family during this difficult period.

Morris’s body arrived in Madang from Lae last Friday, allowing family members, friends, and the football community to pay their final respects.

On Saturday, his body was taken to Laiwaden Oval, a significant venue for Madang football, where members of the soccer community gathered to honour his contribution before he departed for Lae.

On Sunday morning, his body departed Lae for Manus Province, his home province, where he will be laid to rest.

Born on June 12, 1962, in Manus Province, Morris began his education at Nuwok Primary School before attending Manus Provincial High School.

He moved to Madang in 1980 and began working with the Department of Finance and Treasury at the Madang Provincial Administration Headquarters. Through dedication and commitment, he eventually rose to the position of Budget Officer.

Beyond his professional career, Morris developed a strong passion for music and soccer. He represented Madang Province and Papua New Guinea in football before retiring from playing in 1990 to begin his coaching career.

His transition into coaching marked the beginning of a long journey of mentoring and developing young football talents in Madang, Lae, and other parts of Papua New Guinea.

To many players, Morris was more than a coach.

He was a mentor, a father figure, a leader, and a friend who instilled discipline, teamwork, respect, and commitment in young people under his guidance.

“Football brought him to the field, but his passion, leadership, and kindness made him family to generations of players," Beschel said.

His influence extended beyond the football field, with many of the players he mentored becoming part of his extended family.

Morris’ contribution to football went beyond the games he played and the teams he coached. He dedicated himself to helping young people develop their sporting abilities while teaching them important values that extended into their everyday lives.

“A great coach is remembered not only for the games he won, but for the lives he changed.

His years of service helped shape the football community in Madang and beyond, earning him respect from players, officials, clubs, and supporters.

As tributes continue to flow in from the football community, Morris will be remembered for his dedication to the game, his commitment to developing young players, and the lasting impact he made on football in Papua New Guinea.

“His final whistle may have blown, but his legacy will continue to echo across the football fields of Papua New Guinea.”

"His legacy will live on through the players he coached, the clubs he served, and the many lives he touched throughout his journey in football," he added.

item.title: EHP pmv and taxi operators urged to register
item.description: The Eastern Highlands Public Motor Vehicle (PMV) and Taxi Owners Association is urging operators to register with the newly endorsed association and comply with transport laws. Association Chairman Neskefe Aigawa told NBC News that the move follows a rise in unregistered operators, increasing fuel prices and concerns over passenger fares that do not comply with rates set by the Independent Consume
item.content:encoded:
The Eastern Highlands Public Motor Vehicle (PMV) and Taxi Owners Association is urging operators to register with the newly endorsed association and comply with transport laws.

Association Chairman Neskefe Aigawa told NBC News that the move follows a rise in unregistered operators, increasing fuel prices and concerns over passenger fares that do not comply with rates set by the Independent Consumer and Competition Commission (ICCC).

Aigawa noted that a growing number of PMV buses and taxis are operating across Eastern Highlands Province without proper registration and regulation.

He explained that the association would help register operators, address concerns over passenger fares and fuel prices, and promote compliance with transport laws.

Aigawa confirmed that the Eastern Highlands Provincial Government is supporting the initiative, including plans to introduce identification stickers for registered PMVs and taxis.

“The provincial government is supporting this initiative, and we plan to introduce identification stickers for registered PMVs and taxis to help identify operators and ensure they comply with transport regulations,” he said.

He also revealed that the new chairman of the Provincial Land and Licensing Board Committee had assured the association of support, including providing office space and assisting with the numbering of PMVs and taxis.

“The Eastern Highlands PMV and Taxi Operators sticker will serve as an identity for registered PMV and taxi services in the province,” Aigawa said.

Meanwhile, Eastern Highlands Provincial Police Commander Chief Superintendent Albert Beli has warned PMV and taxi operators to comply with government fare regulations and transport laws.

Beli explained that police would work with the Road Traffic Authority to inspect vehicles and impound those that fail to meet roadworthiness and transport requirements once a designated impound area is available.

“If vehicles have faulty tyres, defective signal lights and other mechanical problems, we will get them and park them in one place. Drivers must have proper licences, and bus crews must also meet the required requirements.

“We will park the vehicles there until the owners fix the defects, and only then can they take the vehicles back onto public roads,” Beli said.

The association’s first meeting with PMV and taxi operators has been rescheduled for the 27th at the Goroka Council Chambers. Aigawa is urging operators to attend and comply with transport laws to avoid penalties.

item.title: NBC Western back on air after seven years
item.description: Radio coverage in Western Province is set to reach more communities, with NBC Western’s restored broadcast service extending to Morehead, Kondobol, Balimo and Wipim. NBC Western’s local radio service had been off air since June 2019 after its transmitter was mounted on a Telikom tower that was later decommissioned. The service has now been restored with the transmitter relocated to a PNG Sustainab
item.content:encoded:
Radio coverage in Western Province is set to reach more communities, with NBC Western’s restored broadcast service extending to Morehead, Kondobol, Balimo and Wipim.

NBC Western’s local radio service had been off air since June 2019 after its transmitter was mounted on a Telikom tower that was later decommissioned. The service has now been restored with the transmitter relocated to a PNG Sustainable Development Program (PNGSDP)-owned tower.

The expanded coverage follows a K1.8 million investment by PNGSDP to upgrade FM transmission infrastructure in Daru and install relay equipment in the four remote communities.

PNGSDP Chief Executive Officer Lesieli Taviri said the project took a year of planning and coordination to complete.

“Through an investment of K1.8 million, SDP partnered with NBC to upgrade the FM transmission infrastructure in Daru and install relay equipment on four SDP-owned towers at Morehead, Kondobol, Balimo and Wipim. Delivering this work required careful planning and coordination over one full year,” Ms Taviri said.

She said the partnership combines NBC’s broadcasting mandate and technical expertise with PNGSDP’s investment and delivery support.

Ms Taviri said the agreement also provides for PNGSDP to recover its investment through airtime provided by NBC over several years. The airtime will be used to share information about PNGSDP programs in agriculture, education, health and other areas that support communities.

She said the restored service would also give the Western Provincial Government and other partners another channel to share information with the people.

“The restored service also provides a channel for the Provincial Government and other partners to communicate with our people. SDP is pleased to work with NBC to bring back the Voice of the Sunset to the people of Western Province,” she said.

NBC Managing Director Kora Nou said the resumption of local broadcasting from the Daru station was made possible through the partnership and funding support from PNGSDP.

“Such positive outcomes are the end result of stakeholders working with the NBC to bring broadcast services closer to our people.

“This is a hugely positive development; and I acknowledge the ongoing support of the SDP that has now enabled NBC Western to resume local broadcast from our studio in Daru.

“As much as we try, NBC alone cannot continue to effectively deliver this important national service; we need all key stakeholders to partner with us,” Mr Nou said.

Mr Nou also highlighted the importance of reliable communication during the prevailing El Niño conditions.

“With the effects of El Niño being felt in communities, access to timely and reliable information is critical. NBC’s provincial stations play an important role in communicating public advisories and emergency information, helping communities stay informed and prepared,” he said.

He said strong provincial broadcasting services would also be important ahead of the 2027 National General Elections.

“As we prepare for the 2027 general elections, strong provincial broadcasting services will again be crucial in ensuring people have access to public information, civic education, and election-related awareness,” Mr Nou said.

Meanwhile, NBC’s 95.5 FM signal reaches as far as Kiunga, Tabubil, Ningerum, Telefomin and Olsobip. The signal is also received across the Torres Strait Islands, including Saibai, Boigu, Dauan and Stephen Island, as well as coastal villages extending to Bula.

item.title: East New Britain residents urged to report El Nino impacts
item.description: The public in East New Britain has been urged to report all El Niño-related incidents to their respective District Administrators. The District Administrators are heading emergency centres established in the province’s four districts and are responsible for relaying reports to the Provincial Emergency Operating Centre [PEOC] in Kokopo.
item.content:encoded:
The public in East New Britain has been urged to report all El Niño-related incidents to their respective District Administrators.

The District Administrators are heading emergency centres established in the province’s four districts and are responsible for relaying reports to the Provincial Emergency Operating Centre [PEOC] in Kokopo.

Provincial Administrator and Provincial Disaster Committee Chairman Levi Mano said the PEOC, located at the Disaster Office at Kokopo Fire Station, had been activated recently to coordinate the province’s El Niño response.

He said the centre would work with relevant emergency service providers, including ambulance services, fire services and security forces, to ensure appropriate responses to reported incidents.

However, most response activities will be carried out by the respective district administrations, the National Disaster Centre and the National Treasury Department.

Meanwhile, ward recorders have been tasked with completing a standardised reporting form to monitor the effects of El Niño on water supplies, food availability and community health.

The Ward El Niño Drought Water and Food Daily Assessment Format is designed to provide daily information on conditions in affected communities, helping authorities plan responses and allocate resources where they are needed.

At a meeting held at the PEOC last week, District Administrators and Local Level Government [LLG] Managers submitted updated data on affected households and populations across their respective wards and LLGs.

Deputy Provincial Administrator Danley Puapena said some wards were yet to submit their updated information.

“Our technical team will update and get us through the baseline data we have so that the budget and program for K2.5 million at each district is framed and allocated according to baseline data we have to date,” Mr Puapena said.

The PEOC stressed that accurate and reliable data was essential before relief assistance could be distributed.

Without verified information, the province would struggle to effectively deploy water trucks, distribute food rations and provide medical assistance to affected communities.

item.title: ​MMDDA advances rural electrification drive across Mendi-Munihu district
item.description: Mendi-Munihu District Development Authority (MMDDA) continues to expand power grid connectivity to remote communities across the district. ​Local MP and MMDDA Chairman, Raphael Tonpi announced that people in Heyep, Posulim, and Oleya communities will soon be integrated into the main power grid. This follows the successful electrification of the Wambip, Tulum, and Wei villages in earlier phases of
item.content:encoded:
Mendi-Munihu District Development Authority (MMDDA) continues to expand power grid connectivity to remote communities across the district.

​Local MP and MMDDA Chairman, Raphael Tonpi announced that people in Heyep, Posulim, and Oleya communities will soon be integrated into the main power grid. This follows the successful electrification of the Wambip, Tulum, and Wei villages in earlier phases of the rollout.

​“Connecting one village at a time is the most effective way forward,” MP Tonpi stated, reaffirming the MMDDA's systematic approach to delivering vital utilities to rural households.

​He said the ongoing electrification initiative is being delivered through a partnership involving the MMDDA, the Southern Highlands Provincial Government, Kumul Petroleum Holdings Limited (KPHL), and the Japan International Cooperation System (JICS).

In a parallel effort supported by the Japanese Government, 500 households in Mendi-Munihu were recently connected through a joint venture between the MMDDA and the JICS.

MP Tonpi revealed that grid extension work will expand deeper into remote areas. Planned targets include the Pingirip and Sengso communities within the Bush Karinz area, as well as the stretch from the Injed turn-off to Bim mountain along the Southern Highlands–Enga border.

He stressed that connections are also planned for Penrenz Hiri near the Hela Province boundary.

​“Our goal is simple: we want all our people to have access to electricity,” Tonpi emphasized.

The MP emphasized that reliable electricity will serve as a catalyst for local economic development. It is expected to stimulate Small to Medium Enterprises (SMEs), unlock new income-generating opportunities, and boost household livelihoods across the district.

"​Furthermore, access to power will significantly improve public service delivery. Schools will be able to utilize modern educational technologies and upgraded facilities, while rural health centers will gain the capability to deliver continuous, 24/7 medical care," he said.

He encourage the people of Mendi-Munihu to safeguard these vital public assets and leverage the access to power to elevate our standard of living.
